title: Optimizing windowed arithmetic for quantum attacks against RSA-2048
problem: Quantum factoring algorithms require expensive modular exponentiation circuits; windowed arithmetic trades space for time but still has high uncomputation costs in memory lookups.
motivation: Reducing quantum circuit complexity for cryptanalysis is essential for assessing cryptographic security post-quantum era; even modest gate reductions compound across large circuits.
method: Introduces optimizations to windowed arithmetic for quantum modular exponentiation. Key innovation is reducing uncomputation costs of memory lookups by ~50% through specialized techniques. Enables approximate 50% cost reduction for memory uncomputation in factoring, reducing overall gate count by 1.5-3.4% depending on RSA key size, with optional 16% runtime reduction at 12% qubit overhead.
key_novelty: First comprehensive optimization of uncomputation costs in windowed arithmetic for quantum factoring, achieving 50% reduction in memory lookup uncomputation.
contributions: ~50% reduction in memory lookup uncomputation costs
1.5-3.4% improvement in quantum factoring gate count (RSA-2048)
16% runtime reduction option with 12% qubit overhead trade-off
Generalizable to any windowed arithmetic quantum algorithm

metrics.speedup: 1.5-3.4% gate reduction; 16% runtime at 12% qubit cost

limitations: Evaluation focuses on RSA-2048; applicability to other factorization approaches or post-quantum cryptographic attacks not discussed.
primary_theme: quantum circuit optimization for RSA factoring
